correctness.rationale: The projected creation operators anticommute on compatible additions and both orders vanish for incompatible additions, so Q²=0. On every E>0 eigenspace the parity-odd operator (Q+Q†)/√E is an involution, hence W_n is the signed independence count and |W_n| lower-bounds the total zero-energy multiplicity. A three-column transfer closes with exactly the outer step-one and inner step-three exclusions, and weights every labelled configuration exactly once in tr(Tⁿ). Independent replay `python /workspace/branches/independent_math.py witten` used only the 22 triples with admissible outer neighbors, obtaining the nonzero factors z²−z+1 and z⁵−z+1 exactly. The omitted states cannot belong to a closed walk. Newton sums reproduced every trace for n=7,…,24, and explicit graph checks summing over top-cycle masks reproduced n=7,…,14. Exact root counts give one root in each claimed complex box and its conjugate, all with modulus <11/10, and a real root in (−6/5,−7/6). This accounts for degree five. The rational inequality (7/6)^25>4(11/10)^25+2 persists after normalizing by (7/6)^n because both error terms then decrease. The strict parity sign follows for n≥25 and the exact list covers n=7,…,24 (parity sign from n=13). Dominance gives the stated index asymptotic and log(ρ)/2 lower rate per vertex. This is not a calculation of the full cohomology or an equality for the ground-state multiplicity.

value.rationale: The parity index in a supersymmetric graph model can vanish despite zero modes. Proving its nonvanishing for every simple step-three size is stronger than an isolated finite count or the existence of an exact transfer prescription. The explicit growth rate additionally certifies exponentially many zero-energy states in a natural infinite family without a ground-state classification.
